item.title: Brock Purdy earns comparison to four-time Super Bowl champion from NFL analyst
item.description: Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images Brock Purdy has had an impressive rise since being selected as the final pick in the 2022 NFL draft by the San Francisco 49ers. Four years later, Purdy is firmly in the MVP conversation and his team are in great form, most recently beating the Washington Commanders 23-17. Brock’s rise has been slow, but not every player in the NFL who goes on to be great joins the league with the highest expectations. One example of that is Joe Montana, who ended up going on to win four Super Bowls after being drafted in the third round with the 82nd overall pick back in 1979. Brock Purdy compared to Joe Montana Now, when speaking to CBS, NFL analyst Pete Prisco has made the comparison between Purdy and Montana. He said: “He’s [Purdy] got a killer instinct and he might not look like it, but he does. Joe Montana never looked like it either. But they did. “And where was Joe Montana drafted? In the third round. He didn’t come in, everybody saying he’s going to be a great player, with first round pick ‘Oh, I’m it’. “He worked at it. Brock Purdy was the last player picked. You talk about his work ethic, he’s got to prove to people he belongs. Well, he’s not only proved to people he belongs. He’s proved to people that he excels at it.” The 49ers have not won the Super Bowl in the 21st century, losing in their last three appearances. But they are 6-0 this season and with Purdy and many of his teammates in top form, fans may believe that this season will be their time to break that unwanted streak. item.title: Patriots playoff picture: How beating the Jets impacts the AFC standings
item.description: Their early-season slump firmly in the rear-view mirror, the New England Patriots have started stacking wins. The latest came on Sunday against the New York Jets, a 26-19 victory that improved the team’s record to 4-2 on the year and created some cushion between itself and its rivals. It also helped New England manifest its position in the standings. Let’s take a look. AFC East standings Buffalo Bills (5-1) New England Patriots (4-2) New York Jets (2-4) Miami Dolphins (0-5) The Bills didn’t quite blow the doors off the Raiders like the Patriots did the previous week, but their 33-30 victory was nonetheless enough to keep them in first place in the AFC East. The Patriots are only one game behind, though, because they currently are in possession of the ever-important head-to-head advantage. They won’t be able to use it to take the division lead this week, though. Even if the Patriots beat the Bears on Thursday night, the Bills will stay ahead while on their bye. The Dolphins will be coming off of theirs this week, and try to get their first win of the season against the Jets. Needless to say, a New York loss would be a major blow to the team’s already faint hopes of making noise in the division and the conference as a whole this year. AFC playoff standings Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) Buffalo Bills (5-1) Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) Cleveland Browns (4-2) New England Patriots (4-2) Denver Broncos (4-2) Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2) On the bubble: 8. Baltimore Ravens (4-2), 9. Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) , 10. Las Vegas Raiders (3-3), 11. New York Jets (2-4), 12. Indianapolis Colts (2-4), 13. Houston Texans (2-4 ), 14. Tennessee Titans (1-5) Not yet eliminated, but let’s be real here: 15. Miami Dolphins (0-5), 16. Los Angeles Chargers (0-6) The Ravens and Jaguars losing their respective games to the Browns and Texans shook up the playoff standings in the AFC. While the Chiefs remain on top while on their own bye, the Bills jumped from fourth to second. Jacksonville fell just one spot, while Baltimore dropped all the way down to eighth. The Patriots, meanwhile, are still the top-ranked among the non-division-leading 4-2 teams. Their 4-1 record in conference games gives them an advantage, they hold the head-to-head edge over the Steelers, and they additionally have the highest strength of victory among all teams in the AFC right now.

item.title: Sports doctor reveals what makes ‘zero sense’ about Jalen Hurts’ blood clot injury
item.description: Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles’ medical staff is under fire for how they handled Jalen Hurts’ superficial blood clot. Jalen Hurts was diagnosed with a superficial blood clot during the Philadelphia Eagles’ matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. Initially, the injury was brushed off as nothing major, but Hurts is now out for the remainder of the 2026-27 NFL season. Details have emerged about the Eagles reportedly keeping Hurts awake for 36 hours and still letting him start against the Jaguars despite his condition, and this has one sports doctor completely bewildered. Brian Sutterer is stunned Philadelphia Eagles allowed Jalen Hurts to play after ‘sleep deprivation’ Sports doctor Brian Sutterer is among many who are angry with the Eagles’ handling of Hurts’ blood clot, as he claimed that the organization not allowing him to sleep made ‘zero sense.’ “Ok this part makes zero sense and now I do question why he played after seeing this part of the report. That much sleep deprivation can have a similar effect to being drunk in terms of awareness and neuromuscular control. “There’s nothing inherently dangerous about sleeping while having a superficial clot. Immobility (venous stasis) can cause clots to get worse, but that’s why you are often advised to just sleep with the leg elevated,” Sutterer wrote on X. He added, “I’ve never heard of someone being told to avoid sleep after a superficial blood clot diagnosis, and the short-term effect of that sleep deprivation is a terrible thing to play football with.” Considering football is a contact sport, playing without sleeping put Hurts at massive risk for worsening his condition. Moreover, the Eagles still ended up losing the game 19-17, and if the decision puts Hurts’ future NFL career at risk, it could lead to massive outrage from football fans. There appeared to be no way back for the Leeds academy graduate at City. He has been written off as a £42 million ($56m) flop, on the back of a 2022 transfer, with a star that once illuminated Euro 2020 with the England national team fading badly across recent campaigns. Phillips does have Premier League and Champions League winners’ medals to his name, but tumbled out of favour quickly under Pep Guardiola at the Etihad. Moves to Sheffield are intended to bring a smile back to his face, with a seriously testing period having been endured. [Kevin] De Bruyne, Rodri, in front of you, [Bernardo] Silva. “It was the wrong move for him. Great, you make a load of money and you might have a few medals, but he's not been involved. item.title: Tuesday ‘Dawg Bites Is Ready To Move On
item.description: ATHENS, GA - OCTOBER 17: Georgia's mascot UAG on the sideline during the college football game between the Auburn Tigers and the Georgia Bulldogs on October 17th, 2026, at Sanford Stadium in Athens, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to Tuesday, Bulldog fans! I admit the enthusiasm for attacking this day is lacking, likely the lingering effects of losing to an average Auburn team missing it’s best defender. The reasons for that loss are plain to see: giving the Barners 3 free possessions, extending their drives with huge chunk 15 yard penalties, and most importantly just not executing a game plan as well as they did. But this is ‘Dawg Bites, news and notes about your Georgia Bulldogs, not deep cut game analysis. Plus you’re probably as sick of reliving Saturday afternoon as I am. So let’s see what we can dig up to discuss: Fresh on the heels of do-everything Braylon Miller committing to the “G” this weekend, Bulldog DL Coach Tray Scott picked up his own good news. Forsyth, GA native and current Northwest Mississippi CC defensive lineman Christian Mays announced he was decommiting from Tennessee and coming home. 🚨🚨 BREAKING 🚨🚨 The No. 1 JUCO defensive tackle in the nation, Christian Mays, has flipped from Tennessee to Georgia. Georgia now has the No. 1 AND No. 2 JUCO players committed. https://t.co/roqy32pD5P pic.twitter.com/ZfbOX5bwMJ — Radi Nabulsi (@RadiNabulsi) October 19, 2026 No Monday Kirby Smart press conference because of the off-week, so there’s very little news from the football offices. One can imagine what practice is like on Bloody Tuesday. Perhaps not quite so severe, based on the injuries piling up faster than Auburn students retracting their transfer applications to Grand Canyon University. So we turn Beyond The Hedges, to the pitch, as the Women’s Soccer team finished the regular season home schedule with a much needed win against Missouri. The Volleyball team visited Red Stick, and came away with a 5 set victory . The Spike Dawgs are 6-1 in conference, and 14-3 overall, and positioning themselves for a post-season run. Let’s play 2 (times the normal amount of innings)! . The Georgia baseball team faced Clemson in a fall exhibition Sunday at Foley Field, and ground the visiting Tigers 16-4 over the 18 inning scrimmage. At least some Bulldogs defeated Tigers clad in orange in Athens this weekend. Women’s Tennis are finishing up a tournament in Quebec before returning to the Empire State of the South, the Men’s Golf team are concluding a tourney in Mississippi, while the Women’s Golf Team are starting an event in Tulsa. Maybe following one of these teams can distract you from the matzah ball hanging over our collective memories of Saturday. Yet and still, it’s always a great day to be a Georgia Bulldog. So use the off week to start hating Gators early. And as always… GO ‘DAWGS!!!

item.title: Arch Manning’s bold statement amid rumours of losing Texas’ QB1 spot to backup KJ Lacey Jr.
item.description: Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Texas Longhorns QB Arch Manning addressed the questions around his form and future with some bold responses in his latest press conference. Manning has been held responsible for shrinking when the Longhorns need him most, with the program already losing two games on the season, both being winnable affairs if Manning could have delivered in crunch time. After the Longhorns’ 27-24 loss to Florida on October 17, rumours that coach Steve Sarkisian might bench Manning were rife, with the 22-year-old QB responding emphatically. Arch Manning says all the right things as Texas weigh benching him In his latest press conference, Manning addressed questions around his form and status as starting QB directly. “I fully expect myself to play better. I haven’t put good film on tape for the last five weeks. I am gonna be better, for my teammates, for myself, and for the coach… Losing is never fun; not playing well is never fun. This team is built for adversity; I am built for adversity, and we are gonna respond. I know that… “I feel like I have been a little too hesitant… Like you said, ‘Just let it rip.’ I am gonna die on the hill that I am letting it rip.” Manning’s comments come after a reported decision internally among the Longhorn coaching staff to start giving more first-team reps to backup QB KJ Lacey Jr., signalling that the Longhorns are readying Manning’s backup to step in if he cannot correct his freefall in form. “Sources: Texas is expected to give an uptick in first-team quarterback reps to redshirt freshman KJ Lacey Jr. this week in practice. Arch Manning still projects as the Texas starter. The uptick in Lacey’s reps is a signal that Texas could replace Manning if he continues to struggle.” The Longhorns have a road game against the No. 7-ranked Ole Miss Rebels on October 24, making it a tough test for Manning. However, he needs to step up in a game that important to prove not only that he should remain Texas’ starting QB but also that he belongs in the NFL after the college season is done. Manning has gone 106/166 on pass attempts for 1,295 yards, 11 TDs, and five INTs, with 17 sacks. Despite the raw numbers being decent, Manning ranks near the bottom half for SEC QBs in terms of yards and completions, while his PFF grades have been a letdown. item.title: "Other players have to step up" – Kane reflects on Olise’s absence ahead of "big game" against Arsenal
item.description: "Other players have to step up" – Kane reflects on Olise’s absence ahead of "big game" against Arsenal Bayern Munich will have to manage without star winger Michael Olise when they face Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday, as the Frenchman is suspended after seeing red against Viking FK last week. Although he recognises that Olise’s absence will leave a gap, Harry Kane is confident that other players can step in and make a difference. “When one of your key players is missing, you definitely feel the difference. But that’s exactly when other players have to step up and make the most of this opportunity,” Kane said, as quoted by fcbayern.com. “Whoever plays has to be ready. That’s the nature of the competition at Bayern – and it’s a key factor," said the forward, who added that “everyone trains to an extremely high standard”. "Others can step in and, hopefully, do a really good job,” he underlined. The former Tottenham Hotspur forward is looking forward to a “big game” against the Gunners. “When you’re playing against one of the best teams in Europe, you always have to savour moments like this. We’re up for the challenge. We’re playing here at home – the energy, the fans – it’s sure to be a special night,” the England captain said in the wake of Bayern’s 6-1 win over RB Leipzig at the weekend. “We need to carry the momentum we had in this match into Wednesday’s game. We’re expecting a tough match, so we need to approach it with a clear head. We’re all looking forward to it.” The game between Bayern Munich and Arsenal at the Allianz Arena kicks off on Wednesday at 21:00 CEST.

item.description: Marquinhos and Lamine Yamal [Getty Images] Paris St-Germain v Barcelona - a fixture that could prove to be the most exciting in this season's Champions League. The free-scoring teams start match week three as the league phase's top two, with PSG ahead of Barcelona on goals scored and with no other sides having netted more this term. PSG were 2-1 winners when they met at this stage last season, with Luis Enrique's side going on to win a second successive Champions League title, having also beaten Barcelona over two legs in the quarter-finals three seasons ago. "It will be a fascinating game on Tuesday," French football expert Julien Laurens told BBC Sport's Euro Leagues podcast. Convincing league winners Since the start of the 2025 Club World Cup, Barca and PSG rank second and third respectively for most goals scored per match by clubs in Europe's top five leagues. Barca have netted 192 times in 68 games at a rate of 2.82 per match, with PSG scoring 154 in 67 games at 2.3 per outing. Only Bayern Munich rank above both. Often dubbed the least competitive of the five major European leagues, PSG have dominated French football in recent times. They have won 12 of the past 14 Ligue 1 titles, including the past five. Three of those five were by nine or more points. Barca are defending La Liga champions and have won three of the past four titles. Last season they finished eight points clear of arch rivals and runners-up Real Madrid. PSG became only the second team in the Champions League era to win it in back-to-back seasons, after Real Madrid. In the past two seasons only Bayern from Europe's big five leagues can match Barca and PSG for back-to-back titles. Of the top 14 players on the 2025 Ballon d'Or list, eight of them were current players at PSG or Barcelona. Dembele and team-mate Vitinha finished first and third respectively, with Barcelona teenager Lamine Yamal second. Next Monday's 2026 Ballon d'Or list is also likely to be a similar story. Of the 30 players listed for the award, 13 play for the two clubs. Lamine Yamal, who has eight La Liga goals this season, is among the favourites for this year's award. item.title: Boulter produces emphatic win at Japan Open
item.description: Boulter is 58th in the women's rankings [Getty Images] Katie Boulter claimed a dominant win in her rain-affected first round match against Himeno Sakatsume in the Japan Open. The British player was a set and 3-1 up against the home favourite when play was halted because of bad weather in Osaka on Monday. She completed the win on Tuesday as she secured a 6-3 6-1 victory. "Yesterday was a tough spot to end at," said Boulter, who will play Viktorija Golubic of Switzerland in the second round. "I wanted to play last night and continue but with the rain, unfortunately, that wasn't possible. "It meant that I had to have the same mindset again today and just try to get over the line and focus on getting through the match. "I think I did that. I didn't want to be out here playing a third set so I'm pleased with today." Boulter, 30, took five of nine break points in the match and, even though she faced 13 break points, wild card Sakatsume only managed to take one. Meanwhile, Iga Swiatek's hopes of reaching the WTA Finals in Indian Wells have suffered a setback with the world number nine having withdrawn from the Ningbo Open because of a thigh injury. The Finals, which feature the top eight singles players and doubles teams of the year, is taking place from 8-15 November. item.title: We were not underprepared for World Cup, says England's O'Neill
item.description: Wigan Warriors hooker Brad O'Neill will feature again for England against France [Getty Images] Brad O'Neill has dismissed the suggestion that England were underprepared for their Rugby League World Cup campaign as they bid to start salvaging it with an unchanged team against France this Saturday. England are under pressure - and in huge danger of missing out on a semi-final spot - after losing last Saturday's opening match 30-12 to Tonga, but head coach Brian McDermott has kept faith with the same 19-man squad. McDermott's side have had a tight turnaround for the tournament - the Tonga match was just 14 days after the 2026 Super League Grand Final, with England flying out to Australia 10 days before the game. They did not play a warm-up match - and so went into the game having not played a single international fixture since losing to Australia in Headingley in November last year. Defeat by Tonga came in McDermott's first match in charge since being appointed in April, and O'Neill said they are "new team" and "those little things should come together". But when asked by BBC Sport if England were tired and underprepared for Tonga, the 2026 Super League Man of Steel said: "Not at all, we had a great week of prep heading into the tournament. "The whole team felt really good physically, it was just a good game and the better team won." England men: AJ Brimson, Dom Young, Hugo Savala, Herbie Farnworth, Zach Eckersley, George Williams, Harry Smith, Max King, Brad O'Neill, Luke Thompson, Junior Nsemba, Kai Pearce-Paul, Victor Radley. Interchange: Jez Litten, Ben Currie, Ethan Havard, Sam Walters, Jack Welsby, Matty Ashton. Reserves: Kallum Watkins, Mikey Lewis, Ben Talty. McDermott had said he would "have a look" at team selection after Tonga, but has decided to stick with same XIII for this Saturday's match. He also said England "were not strategically outdone" despite the heavy loss and only needed tweaks rather than a tactical overhaul. "Only having a week together, those little things should come together and we should start executing with practice," said O'Neill. "We're not changing anything we play, it is about the execution side of things. It is those combinations in training and bringing those to the match. "There is a real belief in the team, we are a new team. We need time to work on combos, hopefully those will pay off." AJ Brimson retains his place at full-back in the XIII with Jack Welsby among the interchanges for Saturday's Group B-C match in Perth (kick-off 07:35 BST). Luke Thompson will continue at prop with Morgan Knowles still not fit to play after picking up an injury before the Tonga game. And Mikey Lewis, who was a much-debated pick for the squad as one of the half-backs ahead of 2025 Super League Man Of Steel Jake Connor, remains out of the team. They did not play a warm-up match - and so went into the game having not played a single international fixture since losing to Australia in Headingley in November last year. Defeat by Tonga came in McDermott's first match in charge since being appointed in April, and O'Neill said they are "new team" and "those little things should come together". But when asked by BBC Sport if England were tired and underprepared for Tonga, the 2026 Super League Man of Steel said: "Not at all, we had a great week of prep heading into the tournament. "The whole team felt really good physically, it was just a good game and the better team won." McDermott had said he would "have a look" at team selection after Tonga, but has decided to stick with same XIII for this Saturday's match. He also said England "were not strategically outdone" despite the heavy loss and only needed tweaks rather than a tactical overhaul. "Only having a week together, those little things should come together and we should start executing with practice," said O'Neill. "We're not changing anything we play, it is about the execution side of things. It is those combinations in training and bringing those to the match. "There is a real belief in the team, we are a new team. We need time to work on combos, hopefully those will pay off." And Mikey Lewis, who was a much-debated pick for the squad as one of the half-backs ahead of 2025 Super League Man Of Steel Jake Connor, remains out of the team. Harry Smith will continue alongside England captain George Williams in the half-back roles, despite both being overpowered by Tonga last weekend. Group B-C works as a combined pool of six teams, from which only the top two will reach the semi-finals. England, in Group B, are facing the three teams in Group C - Tonga, France and Papua New Guinea. Qualification gets complicated if teams are level on points: Head-to-head record is the first tiebreaker - which would go against England if they finished level with Tonga. But points difference will be used if two teams in the group have not played each other - which would be the case if England and Samoa needed to be separated. England must win their next two games, against France next Saturday and Papua New Guinea on 30 October, to stand a realistic chance of progression - and because of the World Cup's format, probably need to win them both by a big score. Even then, there is the strong possibility that England will not know their fate for certain until two days after their final match, when Tonga face 2022 finalists Samoa in their last group game. She equalled the record for the most points by an individual England player in a Women's World Cup match. Lucie Sams is named among the interchanges as England take on reigning champions Australia in Perth with kick-off at 10.05 BST - immediately after the men's match. It will be the first time England have played Australia since they suffered their record defeat - 90-4 - in Las Vegas in March 2025. item.title: Pirates Jared Triolo named Gold Glove finalist
item.description: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 2: Jared Triolo #19 of the Pittsburgh Pirates in action during the game against the San Francisco Giants at PNC Park on September 2, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Rawlings has announced the Gold Glove finalists for the 2026 season and the Pittsburgh Pirates’ utility man, Jared Triolo, once again finds himself in the mix. Triolo is one of the three finalists for the National Leagues’ best utility defender, with two-time American League Gold Glove winner Maricio Dubon and Ildemaro Vargas being the other two up for the award. Since the addition of utility defenders being added to the award list, Triolo has been a finalist all three times. 2024 was the inaugural season in which utility players were recognized for the award, and Triolo was the National League’s first utility man to win a Gold Glove. 2026 was another stellar year for Triolo where he was was far in a way the best defender on the Pirates. He was incredible at shortstop in place of rookie Konnor Griffin who missed extensive amounts of time due to injury. At short Triolo racked up 4 DRS across 527.2 innings. He also saw a significant amount of time at third base and totaled 5 DRS in 260.1 innings. Triolo’s 5 DRS at third is just one short of the other two finalists’ totals. Not much gets by him. 🔒 Jared Triolo is up for another Gold Glove! pic.twitter.com/JZIsprWRBC — Pittsburgh Pirates (@Pirates) October 14, 2026 Although he spent the majority of his time on the left side of the infield Triolo also made eight appearances at first base, six in right field and one in center. Third base was where he was rated the highest as a defender with his +5 DRS, a .975 fielding percentage and just two errors at the hot corner. Triolo and Dubon have both received the award in the past, while this is Vargas’ first time finishing as a finalist for the award. The Pirates have two players receiving consideration for the award as second baseman Brandon Lowe is also a finalist in the NL. Staff writer Ethan Coulehan wrote a piece on Lowe and his stellar defensive season. The winners will be announced on November 1.

item.title: Jota returns to Celtic Park after 18-month battle with injury and 'demons'
item.description: Jota returns to Celtic Park after 18-month battle with injury and 'demons' Jota stepped back onto the Celtic Park pitch on Sunday, coming on at half-time as Celtic cruised to a 7-1 win over Hearts. For the 27-year-old, it marked a significant moment after 18 months of physical and mental struggles. His ordeal began in April 2025 at Tannadice, where he suffered cruciate ligament damage just as Celtic secured the title. But his road back had already been complicated by difficult spells at Rennes and Al Ittihad, where foreign-player quotas left him unable to play. The long spell on the sidelines also took its toll mentally. Jota has spoken openly about wrestling with his “demons” and experiencing some very dark moments when he struggled to see a way forward. Looking back now, though, he sees those experiences as part of a process of growth. He says he has learned to live with those inner demons to the point where he can now look back and even laugh. His return to first-team football began last weekend, when he featured in a 2-0 win over Motherwell. The winger is still being eased back into action, however, and has not been included in Celtic’s Europa League squad for the upcoming meeting with Celta Vigo in Glasgow.

item.title: Real Reason For Montez Ford's WWE Absence After Recent Lawsuit (WWE News)
item.description: WWE Recent news has Street Profits star Montez Ford in legal hot water stemming from a "lap dance" involving security on Raw . However, WrestleVotes reported during a Q&A with fans that Ford's continued absence from WWE TV has less to do with that and more do with something else. Namely, he and Bianca Belair just welcomed a baby boy into the world on 4 August. Whilst it's definitely true that security guard Noel Lucas has taken Ford and WWE to court due to an incident on the flagship, WrestleVotes claims there's no lingering heat on Montez and going AWOL from programming isn't some sort of "punishment". The Lucas trial is a messy situation WWE will want to tidy up as soon as possible though. The company actually tried to keep things under wraps for as long as possible - " This lawsuit was kept as quiet as it could be before it broke". item.title: ‘Sick of…’ – Stephen A. Smith boldly reveals what John Harbaugh should tell Cam Skattebo
item.description: Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images Stephen A. Smith weighed in on the Cam Skattebo situation with the New York Giants, telling coach John Harbaugh how he should have dealt with it. Cam Skattebo burst onto the scene in 2025 as an unexpected rookie contributor for the New York Giants. The running back rushed for 410 yards and five touchdowns while adding 207 receiving yards and two scores in just eight games. Injury cut his season short, but not before he became a firm fan-favourite. Skattebo’s personality has as much to do with his popularity as his talent. He has shown himself to be quite straightforward and dynamic, both on the field and off it. But this season, the on-field part of it has been difficult. Skattebo wasn’t given a single touch in NY’s Week 6 loss, largely thanks to his numerous issues with ball security since his return. Stephen A. Smith reveals he is sick of Cam Skattebo, says his production doesn’t match his issues The young running back has fumbled the football four times in six games while averaging just 3.6 yards per carry for New York so far this season. He lost his starting role to Najee Harris, which became a big point of conversation, although Skattebo did accept fault for his mistakes, too. John Harbaugh made his disappointment clear through his decisions. Stephen A. Smith has used words to send both the Giants star and his coach a message. “The Giants are not good enough to have a decent player out there, who is your RB1 and he never touches the football,’ Stephen A. said on First Take. “Having said that, John Harbaugh, let me look in the camera and say this to this former Super Bowl championship coach. What you should have done is say that it was intentional. “Because you’re sick of Cam Skattebo. Because guess what, I am too. And I mean this respectfully. That brother can play, and I wish him all the best. But the backflips… You get an injury and then in the offseason you’re on some stage and you’re backflipping again. “You’re feeling yourself, you’ve got all these commercials, these endorsements, stuff like that. But John Harbaugh needs you to step up on the field. There is such a thing as cats getting a level of popularity that their level of production hasn’t measured up to. That’s the situation with Cam Skattebo.” Considering that Skattebo is still quite young and coming off major injury, he should likely be cut a little more slack than Smith is here. The NFL can be unforgiving, though, so the running back needs to work hard to get back into his coach’s good graces soon. item.title: Ten Hag reveals he wanted to bring Harry Kane to Manchester United from Tottenham
item.description: Ten Hag reveals he wanted to bring Harry Kane to Manchester United from Tottenham Three years ago, Bayern Munich signed Harry Kane from Tottenham Hotspur for a reported fee of €95 million. The German champions were not the only club interested in Kane at the time, with Erik ten Hag revealing that he wanted to bring the striker to Manchester United during the same transfer window. Speaking to The Athletic, the former Manchester United manager revealed that he told the club’s hierarchy that Kane was his preferred target up front. “I said to them, ‘I want only one player — and you know who’," ten Hag said. “I fought for it. I heard that he was very positive, but I never spoke with him about the issue." Ultimately, the club’s management decided against pursuing the deal. “They came to the conclusion. I don’t have the insights in the financials," the Dutchman said. Ten Hag managed Manchester United from the summer of 2022 until October 2024.

item.title: Week 7 upsets impact college football bowl projections with CFP field shuffling
item.description: The College Football Playoff has a different shade of orange after Week 7. Moving out of the field in the latest bowl projections is Texas after its loss to Florida . Moving in is SEC counterpart Tennessee following a spirited win by the Volunteers against Alabama . That, surprisingly, is the only change among the 12 teams selected for the bracket that will determine the national champion despite a slew of upsets during the weekend. Common sense would seem to indicate more adjustments. But with several contenders losing and not a ton of replacement candidates available, there just isn't a lot different to the picture except for the seedings. The second half of the season is shaping up to have many twists and turns. The losses by SEC contenders increase the likelihood of 9-3 teams being in the mix for at-large spots. Those teams could be competing with one- or two-loss teams from the ACC and Big 12 in what should be a challenging situation for the committee. That debate is for another day. There's still a long way to go. item.description: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s continued absence from India’s playing XI has left fans frustrated, but former India spinner Murali Kartik believes there is little reason for the team management to rush the 15-year-old into the side when the established opening options are performing well. Despite being named Player of the Series during India’s tour of Zimbabwe, Sooryavanshi did not feature in the subsequent T20I series against Afghanistan and West Indies. The teenage batter is also yet to make his senior India debut on home soil, even as his performances in the IPL have made him one of the country’s most talked-about young talents. His absence has become a talking point at India’s home matches, with supporters hoping to see him play. Sooryavanshi did get an opportunity to open alongside Abhishek Sharma during the Asian Games, offering a glimpse of his potential, but his wait for a regular spot in the senior team’s playing XI continues. Speaking in an interaction facilitated by Sony Sports Network, Kartik backed the management’s decision to retain its existing opening combination, highlighting the contributions of Sanju Samson and Abhishek. He also pointed to the presence of Ishan Kishan, whose recent form has made competition for a place at the top of the order even tougher. "I am not somebody who makes a change for the sake of it. So, when it comes to the opening duo in India, I know they are a bit inconsistent, but that is what has won games for you," said Karthik. Samson and Abhishek have accumulated 1,125 runs together in 38 T20Is, making them India’s fourth-highest run-scoring partnership in the format. item.title: Scott Frost believes 24-team CFP expansion will be 'even more competitive'
item.description: ORLANDO — Expansion of the College Football Playoff to a field of 24 teams appears imminent and inevitable, a development that UCF head coach Scott Frost believes will make the postseason more competitive than ever. "I'd just like to be there someday," Frost said Oct. 19 during his game-week availability ahead of the Knights ' home date with No. 2 BYU. "I don't really think my opinion matters much in terms of that. I heard Coach (Nick) Saban , the most successful that's ever done it, say that there wasn't 24 deserving teams to be in it. I kind of think there is this year." Frost pointed to the recent string of surprising results, including five teams ranked in the AP's top 10 falling this past weekend. Georgia and Texas fell at home to unranked opponents — Auburn and Florida, respectively. BYU, a double-digit underdog, snapped Notre Dame 's 16-game winning streak in a prime-time showdown. Ohio State got its revenge against defending champion Indiana, and Tennessee throttled Alabama for the Crimson Tide's second straight defeat. "I think it will be even more competitive than it's ever been," Frost added. "Sure want to be in it someday, but I think it's going to be great for people to watch." Expansion should give the Big 12 Conference greater equity than it has received in the 12-team format. Each of the past two seasons, the Big 12 has been a one-bid league with only its champion earning the automatic invitation — Arizona State in 2024 and Texas Tech last year. BYU's victory raised the national perception of the Big 12, as did Oklahoma State's stunning victory over then-No. 6 Oregon last month. Four of the league's teams — BYU, Texas Tech, Utah and Houston — are among the top 16 in this week's US LBM Coaches Poll , for which Frost is a voter. As for the argument of devaluing college football's regular season at the cost of playoff expansion, Frost still thinks games will matter a great deal each week. "People show up for NFL games, and that's a 17-game season where each game matters even a little less," Frost said. "It's going to be hard, in the Playoff, to be considered if you're not at least a 10-2 team. So every game matters. "I'm kind of a traditionalist, and I grew up with it a certain way. And it's changing. We all have to get on board with that. You can't tell me that each game doesn't matter right now, and I don't think a 24-team (bracket) is going to change that." item.title: Tacko Fall, UCF's 7-foot-6 legend, returns to NBA with Philadelphia 76ers
item.description: ORLANDO — Former UCF basketball star Tacko Fall returns to the NBA after a nearly five-year absence, signing a two-way contract with the Philadelphia 76ers over the weekend. Fall inked an Exhibit 10 deal last month, a one-year, non-guaranteed, NBA minimum salary contract that allows a team to evaluate a player during training camp or the preseason while securing their G League affiliate rights. Injuries to Philly's frontcourt, including the season-long loss of projected backup center Ariel Hukporti (Achilles), opened a roster spot. The 30-year-old Fall, listed at 7-foot-6 and 299 pounds, last played an NBA game during the 2021-22 campaign with the Cleveland Cavaliers. He has played 37 times across parts of three seasons, averaging 2.2 points, 2.4 rebounds and 0.8 blocks per game. "I was a little speechless, to be honest," Fall told reporters over the weekend. "Like I said, I've had quite a few challenges since I left, and when you get that, after all these years and after all the hard work, I think it means a lot more, for sure. "I'm excited to be back. I feel like this is a great opportunity, and with the things that I can do, I believe that I can really help this team. And for me, whatever they need me to go out there and do, I'm going to do, come in with great energy and just do what I can do to help." Johnny Dawkins , who coached Fall for three seasons at UCF and played five years for the 76ers , is thrilled to see him given another shot in the NBA. Fall most recently played for the Ningbo Rockets of the Chinese Basketball Association. "It's well deserved," Dawkins said. "Tacko's a terrific human being … but also, he's an NBA player. He has the mobility, and he has the size. I know the game has changed so much with bigs shooting 3s and all those things. I keep waiting for the game to get a new iteration where we go back to throwing it in the post to guys. "Maybe that will be it with Embiid and him on the same roster." Fall holds UCF's all-time Division I program record in field goal percentage (.740) and blocked shots (280), while ranking third in rebounds (887). He started 33 games as the Knights earned an at-large bid into the 2019 NCAA Tournament. The 76ers travel to Madison Square Garden for the second game of the 2026-27 NBA season, squaring off with the defending champion New York Knicks . Philadelphia made two of the biggest moves of the offseason, signing LeBron James as a free agent and acquiring Jaylen Brown via trade from the Boston Celtics. Brown and Fall were teammates in Boston in both the 2019-20 and 2020-21 seasons. They join a roster that already boasted a pair of All-Stars: center Joel Embiid and guard Tyrese Maxey. item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied Usually, the second weekend of October sees Christian Pulisic flanked by compatriots as the Star-Spangled Banner plays. On Sunday, his pre-match music was O Generosa, the Serie A anthem, which he observed with a soft smile. Mark Twain’s first visit to Italy left him describing the country as “a vast museum of magnificence and misery”, and it’s a fitting summary of Pulisic’s three-plus years with Milan. The magnificence: 43 goals and 25 assists in 138 appearances. The misery: just one trophy since he arrived in July 2023, a 2025 Supercoppa Italia held in Saudi Arabia. Continue reading...

item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: Lionel Messi’s Argentina career turned football into a sacred mystery
item.description: Jorge Messi wanted his country to fall in love with his son. That ambition was fulfilled during a brilliant international career that ended this week “What Argentina is doing in this World Cup is of a sacred order,” Brazilian writer Milly Lacombe posted at the height of the tide of anti-Argentinian sentiment during this year’s tournament. She was exploring the contradiction she felt around her support of Lionel Messi: “a player who is a God and a man who shakes Trump’s hand”. Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. How is it possible that Messi was not speaking out against the racist incidents we all saw around the Argentina team , she asked. “That’s why it hurts so much to see someone with Messi’s power choosing to make himself small,” she wrote. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
